question.text: How many votes of no confidence will Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul receive?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of House of Representatives members voting for a motion of no confidence against Thailand's prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in the first such vote being held before December 23, 2026.
question.fine_print: If no such vote takes place before December 23, 2026, the question resolves as **140 or fewer**

research:
I found no sign that the vote has happened yet. It is scheduled for **December 11, 2026**, before the December 23 cutoff. The motion was signed by **145 MPs**. The opposition outside Kla Tham comes to about **143 to 149 seats**, so the likely outcome looks bunched around the 141-144, 145-148 and 149-154 bins, unless Kla Tham MPs cross over or the opposition boycotts.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL is given. The deciding figure is the House of Representatives roll-call tally of no-confidence votes against Anutin specifically, since the motion covers 18 ministers voted on separately. It will be reported by the House and outlets like Bangkok Post, The Nation and Reuters. There is no data series to pull: I found no vote result as of today.
- 2026-10-08: A motion under Section 151 of the Constitution was filed, signed by 145 MPs, targeting Anutin and 17 other Bhumjaithai ministers. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40072840)

## 2. Current status
- The vote has not happened. Nothing settles the question yet.
- 2026-11-03: Reuters reports the whips agreed a December 7-11 timetable, with the vote on Dec 11. The coalition holds 292 seats of 499 and the opposition 207, but that 207 includes Kla Tham's 58, and Kla Tham did not join the motion. [ThePrint/Reuters](https://theprint.in/world/thai-pm-to-face-his-first-censure-debate-in-december/3088890/)
- The Nation says the Cabinet was asked to confirm the dates or consider starting earlier. Another option mentioned was a Dec 6-9 debate with the vote on Dec 10. Either way the vote falls before Dec 23. [Ground News](https://ground.news/article/no-confidence-debate-targeting-18-ministers-likely-set-for-december-6-10)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-21: Gen Z protesters are calling for the government to resign. Anutin says he will listen if the protests stay lawful and plays down fears of escalation. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40073766)
- 2026-11-16: Coffee Parliament expects the government to win easily, says Kla Tham may give Anutin "extra votes", and notes rumours of a Bhumjaithai-Kla Tham merger. [Coffee Parliament](https://www.coffeeparliament.com/p/bhumjaithais-three-pronged-threats)
- 2026-11-01: The Star says ministers from outside parliament face reshuffle risk after the vote. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2026/11/01/thailand039s-outsider-ministers-face-reshuffle-risk-in-censure-vote)
- 2026-10-08: The opposition bloc filing the motion is People's Party plus Democrat, Thai Pakdee, Thai Ruam Palang and Seri Ruam Thai. Kla Tham did not sign, and opposition leader Natthaphong said some members "faced constraints" that kept them from signing. [Asianews](https://asianews.network/?p=306730), [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40072017)
- Seat arithmetic: the 2026 election results were People's Party 120 and Democrat 21, with several one-seat parties. In the March 19 PM vote, People's Party MPs split 118 for Natthaphong, 1 abstention and 1 for Anutin. The Democrats (21) abstained. Thai Ruam Palang (6) voted for Anutin even though it is now listed with the opposition. [Wiki election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Thai_general_election), [Wiki cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Anutin_cabinet)
- On Reuters' figures, the opposition excluding Kla Tham is 207 - 58 = **149**.
- Risk to the People's Party headcount: the Supreme Court is hearing an ethics case against 44 former Move Forward MPs, including 10 sitting People's Party MPs. It did not suspend them, though a petition seeks to suspend Natthaphong. I found no newer ruling. [Thai PBS](https://www.thaipbsworld.com/analysis/into-the-judicial-jaws:-people%E2%80%99s-party-leaders-face-a-familiar-fate), [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/3261893/court-asked-to-suspend-pp-leader)

## 4. Base rates
- In Thai censure votes, the no-confidence tally usually comes in a few votes below the opposition's seat count, because of absences and abstentions.
  - 2021-09: Prayut, 264 for and 208 against, 3 abstentions. [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2176363)
  - 2022-07: Prayut, 256 for and 206 against, 9 abstentions. [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2352327/prayut-10-other-ministers-survive-no-confidence-vote)
  - 2021-02: I recall about 272 to 206 for Prayut, but I did not confirm it this session.
- 2020-02: From memory, not checked this session, Pheu Thai boycotted the vote, so the no-confidence count was very low. This is a precedent for a boycott pushing the result into the lowest bin.
- The PM usually draws the highest no-confidence count among the targeted ministers: in 2021-09 his 208 was the top figure.
- The 145 signatures are a lower bound on the opposition's core. It is unclear whether all 21 Democrat MPs and the 6 Thai Ruam Palang MPs will vote against Anutin.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this vote. None of the markets listed with the question match it: they cover France, Israel, sports and so on.
- Experts agree Anutin will survive comfortably (Reuters analysts, Coffee Parliament). I found no numeric projections of the tally.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Dec 7-10 (or Dec 6-9): the debate. Dec 11 (or Dec 10): the vote.
- Possible swings in the count:
  - Kla Tham (58) could vote with the opposition, abstain, or back the government; reports point to abstaining or backing Anutin.
  - Some Democrat or small-party MPs could abstain.
  - People's Party MPs could be absent or suspended by courts.
  - The opposition could walk out or boycott.
  - The House could be dissolved, or the schedule could slip past Dec 23. That would resolve as "140 or fewer", but there is no sign of either.
- The Gen Z protests are ongoing and could affect the political mood.

I found no vote yet: the House is scheduled to vote on the censure motion on 11 December 2026. The key numbers are 145 MPs signing the motion and an opposition bloc of roughly 149 seats outside Kla Tham. That puts the question near the line between "141-144" and "145-148".

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no data file for this. The result will be the official House tally on the motion against Anutin. The motion targets 18 ministers individually, and each one gets a separate vote.
- 2026-10-28: Whips from the government, the opposition and the Cabinet agreed on a debate from 7 to 10 December and the vote on **11 December 2026**. That is before the 23 December cutoff. The Cabinet still had to confirm the dates. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40072840), [Thansettakij](https://www.thansettakij.com/politics/672452)
- Current value: no vote has happened yet.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The government is expected to survive comfortably. What matters here is the number of yes votes, not whether the motion passes.
- 2026-10-08: The opposition, led by Natthaphong of the People's Party, filed the motion with **145 MP signatures**. Kla Tham did not sign. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40072017)
- 2026-11-02: Reuters, via Yahoo, reports the coalition holds **292 of 499** seats and the opposition **207**. Kla Tham, with 58 MPs, sits outside the coalition and did not join the motion. That implies about **149 non-Kla Tham opposition MPs**. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/thai-pm-face-first-censure-055815512.html)
- The opposition is described as five parties led by the People's Party and including the Democrats. [The Standard](https://thestandard.co/the-standard-global/no-confidence-debate-pushed-december/)
- Rough makeup, from the 2026 election and the March 2026 PM vote: People's Party about 120 (118 voted for Natthaphong, 1 backed Anutin), Democrats 21, plus single seats such as Thai Liberal, Seri Ruam Thai and Thai Pakdee. In the PM vote, Thai Ruam Palang's 6 MPs backed Anutin. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Anutin_cabinet), [Coffee Parliament](https://www.coffeeparliament.com/p/anutins-second-term-is-confirmed)
- Kla Tham reportedly "signalled its readiness to support the ministers" in the vote. I found no official party statement. In March it abstained in the PM vote. [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/3345936/hat-yai-a-test-for-anutin)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-21: Anutin says the government will listen to the Gen Z protesters demanding its resignation, and plays down fears of unrest. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40073766)
- 2026-11-17: The Supreme Court ethics case against 44 former Move Forward MPs continues. It covers about 10 sitting People's Party MPs, including Natthaphong, who are not suspended. The next hearing is 1 December, and hearings are expected to run to around May 2027, so a ruling before 11 December looks unlikely. [Siamrath](https://siamrath.co.th/politics/336210), [Thai PBS](https://www.thaipbsworld.com/politics/supreme-court-to-decide-fate-of-former-mps-of-defunct-move-forward-party-facing-l%C3%A8se-majest%C3%A9-charges)
- 2026-11-14: Anutin says the government has the votes and will answer with facts. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40073496)
- 2026-11-01: Analysts expect the government to survive. Five "outsider" ministers with weak vote support could face a reshuffle. Debate time: opposition 51 hours, Cabinet 17 hours. [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40073015)
- 2026-10: ACLED calls removal "highly improbable" without major defections. [ACLED](https://acleddata.com/expert-comment/will-thailands-no-confidence-motion-deepen-pressure-anutins-government)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-03-26: Paetongtarn won 319 to **162**, with 7 abstentions. Four of those abstentions were Democrat MPs; the Democrats were then in her government. The People's Party alone held about 143 seats, so the opposition voted close to its full strength. [PRD](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/376418), [Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40047867)
- 2026-03-19: In the PM vote, 116 to 119 MPs voted against Anutin, essentially the People's Party plus one or two others. The Democrats abstained as a bloc, the fourth PM vote in a row they have done so. [Coffee Parliament](https://www.coffeeparliament.com/p/anutins-second-term-is-confirmed)
- Pattern: Thai censure votes usually land at, or a few votes below, the opposition's seat count. In this case:
  - Baseline: about 141 to 149 if the People's Party and Democrats vote together.
  - Lower: about 120 to 125 if the Democrats abstain or split.
  - Higher: 155 or more would need Kla Tham or coalition MPs to vote yes, which looks unlikely given Kla Tham's signals.
- The 145 signatures are the best direct sign of committed votes. Individual absences or abstentions could shift the total by a few.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this. The markets supplied with the question (France, Israel, sports and others) don't match it.
- Experts (Reuters, ACLED, Nation) all expect Anutin to survive. None gives a vote-count forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The Cabinet still has to confirm the schedule. Dates could move, but the vote is currently 11 December, well before 23 December.
- 7 to 10 December: the debate itself, where new revelations could sway Democrats or wavering MPs.
- Possible risks:
  - Kla Tham's final position, or it joining the coalition.
  - Rifts between Pheu Thai and Bhumjaithai. Pheu Thai ministers are not targeted.
  - A dissolution of the House before the vote: I found no current reporting of one.
  - Rulings that remove opposition MPs: none look imminent.
  - Gen Z protests growing.
- If no vote happens before 23 December, the question resolves "140 or fewer".

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The vote is scheduled for about December 10-11, 2026, roughly three weeks away. The result will be known about 12 days before the December 23 cutoff.

(b) **Status quo:** If the vote goes ahead as planned and the opposition bloc that filed the motion votes as a unit, minus the usual few absences, the tally lands around 143-148. That centres on the 145-148 bin.

(c) **Base rates:** In recent Thai censure votes the tally against the PM fell 2-6 below the opposition's nominal seat count.
- 2021-09: Prayut drew 208 no-confidence votes against an opposition of roughly 212 seats.
- 2022-07: Prayut drew 206 against roughly 208-210 seats.
- The PM usually draws the highest tally among the targeted ministers.
- Boycotts (as in 2020) are a rare tail case.
- Applied to an opposition outside Kla Tham of about 149 seats, this gives about 143-147.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-10-08: The motion was filed with 145 signatures. That suggests a committed core of about 145.
- 2026-11-03 (Reuters): The opposition has 207 seats, of which Kla Tham holds 58. That leaves about 149 outside Kla Tham. The vote is set for Dec 11.
- Two parties in the bloc have wavered before. The Democrats (21) abstained in the March PM vote, and Thai Ruam Palang (6) voted for Anutin then.
- 2026-11-16 (Coffee Parliament): Kla Tham may give Anutin "extra votes". That makes large Kla Tham crossovers to the opposition unlikely, though a few individual crossovers are possible.
- Court risks to People's Party MPs exist, but no suspension has been ordered.

(e) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Downside: The Democrats partly abstain, or a court suspends People's Party MPs before the vote. Either could push the tally into the 130s. An opposition walkout or a dissolution of the House would also do this.
- Upside: Gen Z protest pressure pulls a handful of Kla Tham MPs into voting against Anutin. That could push the tally to 150 or more.

**Adjustment:** I start from the base rate centred on 145. There is no matching market to anchor on. I widen the downside because of the history of Democrat and Thai Ruam Palang abstentions. I keep a modest upper tail for possible Kla Tham defections.
